explanation: He wrote it in 1513, after losing his government post and being exiled to his farm. It was published only in 1532, five years after his death, and his name became an adjective.

claims.text: Niccolò Machiavelli of Florence wrote The Prince.
Dante, Lorenzo de' Medici and Galileo did not write The Prince; Machiavelli dedicated it to Lorenzo di Piero de' Medici.
Machiavelli wrote The Prince in 1513, after losing his post in the Florentine government, while banished to his farm outside Florence.
The Prince was published in 1532, five years after Machiavelli's death in 1527.
Machiavelli's name gave English the adjective Machiavellian.
